teaser.en: Long before toothpaste, coastal people cleaned their teeth with a chewed twig from this tree, and many still do.
teaser.sw: Muda mrefu kabla ya dawa ya meno, watu wa pwani walisafisha meno yao kwa kijiti kilichotafunwa cha mti huu, na wengi bado hufanya hivyo.

summary.en: *Msuwaki* is the toothbrush tree, a drooping, pale-leaved shrub of dry bush and riverbanks. Its twigs and roots are the original toothbrush of the coast, and the word *mswaki* now means any toothbrush.
summary.sw: *Msuwaki* ni mswaki, kichaka chenye matawi yanayolegea na majani ya kijani hafifu, cha vichaka vikavu na kingo za mito. Vitawi na mizizi yake ndiyo miswaki ya asili ya pwani, na neno *mswaki* sasa lina maana ya mswaki wa aina yoyote.

about.en: *Msuwaki* is an evergreen shrub or small tree with drooping, sometimes trailing branches. Its leaves are pale green and slightly fleshy. Small pink-purple berries follow the tiny flowers. The twigs and roots have a sharp, peppery taste.
about.sw: *Msuwaki* ni kichaka au mti mdogo wa kijani mwaka mzima wenye matawi yanayolegea, wakati mwingine yakitambaa ardhini. Majani yake ni ya kijani hafifu na yenye majimaji kidogo. Matunda madogo ya rangi ya waridi-zambarau hufuata maua madogo sana. Vitawi na mizizi yake vina ladha kali kama ya pilipili.

where.en: It grows in coastal and dry lowland bushland and along river banks.
where.sw: Huota katika vichaka vya pwani na vya nyanda za chini zilizo kavu, na kando ya kingo za mito.

uses.en: Twigs and roots are used as toothbrushes: the end is chewed until it frays into bristles, and then rubbed over the teeth. The peppery fruit is eaten, the roots and bark are used in traditional medicine, and the leaves are fodder for livestock.
uses.sw: Vitawi na mizizi hutumika kama miswaki: ncha hutafunwa hadi itawanyike kuwa nyuzi kama brashi, kisha husuguliwa juu ya meno. Matunda yake yenye ladha ya pilipili huliwa, mizizi na gome hutumika katika dawa za kienyeji, na majani ni lishe ya mifugo.

culture.en: The tree gave its name to the toothbrush itself: in Swahili, *mswaki* means a toothbrush of any kind, and the chewing stick is still a common sight on the coast.
culture.sw: Mti huu ndio uliotoa jina lake kwa mswaki wenyewe: kwa Kiswahili, *mswaki* ni mswaki wa aina yoyote, na kijiti cha kutafuna bado ni jambo la kawaida kuonekana pwani.

names.en: In Digo it is *msuwaki* or *mswaki*. The Swahili, Giriama and Chonyi name is *mswaki*. In English it is the toothbrush tree; it is also known worldwide as miswak. Pakia notes that another tree, *Dobera loranthifolia*, is also called *msuwaki*.
names.sw: Kwa Kidigo ni *msuwaki* au *mswaki*. Jina la Kiswahili, Kigiriama na Kichonyi ni *mswaki*. Kwa Kiingereza unaitwa *toothbrush tree*; pia unajulikana duniani kote kama *miswak*. Pakia anabainisha kwamba mti mwingine, *Dobera loranthifolia*, pia huitwa *msuwaki*.

reason.en: Horsewood, whose twigs are also used as toothbrushes
reason.sw: *Chinyapala* (*horsewood*), ambao vitawi vyake pia hutumika kama miswaki

reason.en: African myrrh, also used for toothbrushes
Grows in the same dry bushland
